title: Perturbation-Guided 25-Layer HfO2/SiO2 with Forced Layer 3/9/13 Offset
scientific_hypothesis: Forcing deterministic thickness perturbations on layers 3, 9, and 13 by +/- 3.0 nm from their iteration_08 optimized positions will break symmetry-lock on specific optical paths, enabling the gradient optimizer to discover improved phase-matching conditions that increase best_target_score beyond 0.5155.
design_principle: Apply the feedback directive's deterministic perturbation schedule to escape local optima while preserving the verified HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack principle. Increase layer count from 21 to 25 to provide additional degrees of freedom for visible/NIR blocking.
proposed_topology: 25 finite layers: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | Fused silica
design_variables: Initial thicknesses for layers 3, 9, 13 offset by +3.0 nm from iteration_08 best candidate
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional evaporatable dielectrics
Layer thickness tolerance +/- 3.0 nm perturbation is within typical deposition control
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for planar multilayer interference
Quarter-wave stack principle for bandpass filters
Perturbation theory for escaping local optima in gradient-based optimization
expected_advantages: Breaking symmetry-lock may reveal higher-scoring regions of design space
25 layers provide more blocking capability than 21 layers
Deterministic perturbation is reproducible and traceable
known_risks: Perturbation may temporarily reduce target_score before improvement
HfO2 absorption at 255 nm may limit maximum achievable transmission
Increased layer count may reduce robustness_score
execution_request_english: Optimize a 25-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack on fused silica substrate under air incidence for solar-blind UV filter application. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance at 255-280 nm, suppress transmittance at 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. Initialize all layer thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness centered at 267 nm. Before optimization begins, apply deterministic perturbation: add +3.0 nm to initial thickness of layer 3 (HfO2), layer 9 (HfO2), and layer 13 (HfO2). Use gradient_thickness optimizer with standard bounds. Material registry resolves HfO2 and SiO2. Total finite layers: 25. No metal layers. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, run_status, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 255–280 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Transmittance in 300–700 nm; Transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers; No metal layers; Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Applied feedback directive to inject deterministic perturbation on layers 3, 9, 13 (+3.0 nm offset) to break symmetry-lock observed in iteration_08. Increased layer count from 21 to 25 to explore additional design space toward 30-layer limit.
